primary_claim: Chinese open-weight LLMs (Qwen3-32B, GLM-4.5-Air, Minimax-M2.7) show substantially higher average political-bias scores than non-Chinese controls (gpt-oss-20b, Ministral-14B) on a 250-question LLM-judged benchmark, with bias varying widely between Chinese models and sometimes extending to topics unrelated to China.

effect.value: wide spread among Chinese models; qwen3-32b scores far lower than minimax-m2.7

contradicts_or_qualifies: The wide variation in bias score among Chinese models (qwen3-32b far lower than minimax-m2.7) was not consistent with the author's expectation of uniform censorship, suggesting Chinese labs have differing latitude on censorship level
stated_future_work: Use a much larger question set for a more statistically significant benchmark
Create separate questions unrelated to China to more rigorously test whether bias extends beyond China-related topics
Use a more intelligent LLM (e.g. Claude Sonnet) for question generation and judging
limitations_stated: The judge LLM is American, so results reflect difference in bias from American/French models rather than an objective bias measure
The judge LLM (gpt-oss-120b) is from the same family as one control (gpt-oss-20b), which likely biases that control's score favorably
Small-scale, rough experiment performed on a shoestring budget (<~$1 for the judge LLM), limiting model choice
quote: Interestingly, there is a wide range of bias scores in the chinese models, with qwen3-32b scoring far lower than minimax-m2.7.
